method: EMMA continuing-disclosure ANNUAL reports (gold source) + original Official Statement (issuance baseline) per CUSIP; AV/land-use/taxpayer/debt tables read directly from the PDFs (data/os_cache/). Ratios computed; nothing inferred.

291119KP9.name: Emery Unified School District GO (Alameda Co), 3% 2045
291119KP9.concern: office-CRE channel: tiny district, AV concentrated in Emeryville commercial (office/biotech)

av_latest.authority: Emery FY2025 CD Annual Report sec. E (Source: California Municipal Statistics)

av_baseline_issuance.authority: Emery OS p22 Assessed Valuation by Land Use

av_trend_pct.note: 5yr total-AV trend +23.8% (6.333B->7.838B). BUT local-secured FLATTENED in office downturn: FY23-24 6.878B -> FY24-25 7.008B -> FY25-26 7.010B (+0.04% last yr). The office-CRE channel IS showing in the data.

commercial_share.value: Non-residential 56.91% of local secured AV; Commercial/Office ALONE 48.49%; Industrial 6.25%. Residential 43.09% but almost entirely condo/townhouse (25.4%) + apartments (14.5%); single-family only 1.27%.
commercial_share.fiscal_year: 2018-19 (OS land-use table; latest annual omits land-use)

top10_taxpayer_share.no1_to_no10: Pixar 3.86 / KBSIII Towers (office) 3.09 / LMV II (apts) 2.83 / SPUS8 2100 Powell (office) 2.77 / Courtyards at 65th (apts) 2.77 / Emery Station West (office) 2.42 / Avalon Public Market (apts) 2.18 / Bcore Emerytech (office) 1.97 / Bay Center Investor (office) 1.95 / GC Diagnostics (industrial) 1.90
top10_taxpayer_share.authority: Emery FY2025 CD Annual Report sec. G; (1) note: 2025-26 local secured AV 7,010,352,462; top-20 sum 2,909,021,633 = 41.50%; top-10 computed = ~26.4%
top10_taxpayer_share.note: HIGH concentration and office-tilted: 7 of top-10 and the largest names are office buildings. Pixar single-name 3.86%.

go_debt_outstanding.authority: Emery FY2025 CD Annual Report sec. D, GO bonds outstanding table Total = $81,924,743 (Source: District Audit). 7 GO series, base CUSIP 291119, AGM-insured.

av_to_debt_ratio.note: Strong AV-to-debt coverage (~96x); debt is ~1.0% of AV. Even a severe office repricing leaves large cushion.

teeter.authority: Alameda County operates a Teeter Plan; Emery FY2025 CD Annual Report sec. H references the County of Alameda Teeter Plan (no adverse changes noted). Confirmed.
teeter.implication: Teeter = county advances 100% of the levy to the District regardless of taxpayer delinquency, then keeps penalties/interest. Insulates debt-service collections from CRE-tenant delinquency; the residual risk is AV (assessment) decline, not collection timing.

291119KP9.verdict_basis: Concern is REAL and visible: 57% non-residential / 48% office, top-20=41.5%, Pixar #1 -> genuine office-CRE concentration, and local-secured AV has flatlined the last 2 yrs (+0.04% FY25-26). BUT it does not impair the bond: AV-to-debt ~96x (debt only ~1.0% of AV) and Alameda Teeter advances 100% of the levy, so debt service is collected even on delinquent CRE parcels. A catastrophic ~95% AV collapse would be needed to threaten coverage. Hold-to-maturity GO credit intact; flag for ongoing AV monitoring (office channel).

900211CP6.name: Turlock USD SFID No.1 GO (Stanislaus Co), 3% 2043
900211CP6.concern: levy rides on SFID No.1 boundary, not whole district; unknown what is inside it

sources.official_statement: https://emma.msrb.org/EP1036730-EP803276-EP1204805.pdf (SFID No.1 issuance; FY18-19 SFID land-use + largest-taxpayer baseline)

av_latest.authority: Turlock FY2024-25 Annual Report p2 (Source: Stanislaus & Merced County Auditor-Controllers). SFID-SPECIFIC AV is separately disclosed.

av_baseline_issuance.authority: Turlock SFID No.1 OS p16 land-use table

av_trend_pct.note: +42.7% over 7yr (6.07B->8.67B local secured); +3.8% latest year (8.334B->8.665B). Steady Central-Valley growth, no flattening.

commercial_share.value: SFID No.1 is RESIDENTIAL-MAJORITY: Residential 69.91% (single-family 59.74%), Non-residential 30.09% (Commercial/Office 16.90%, Industrial 7.50%, Agricultural/Rural 4.13%). 20,861 parcels, 87.8% residential by count.
commercial_share.note: Diversified, owner-occupied-heavy base. Ag/food-processing tail (Foster Poultry Farms etc.) but small. Opposite profile to Emery.

top10_taxpayer_share.authority: Turlock SFID OS p19 largest-taxpayers; no single taxpayer > 2.35%; top-20 = 11.50% of secured AV
top10_taxpayer_share.note: LOW concentration. Top names span shopping centers, food processing (Foster Poultry, Sensient, Supherb), apartments, medical (Doctors Medical Center), Costco, Lowes. Highly diversified.

go_debt_outstanding.authority: Turlock FY2024-25 Annual Report p2: '$39,518,000 of School Facilities Improvement District No. 1 General Obligation Bonds remain outstanding.'

av_to_debt_ratio.note: SFID AV-to-debt ~230x; debt only ~0.44% of SFID AV. Extremely strong cushion.

teeter.authority: Turlock FY2024-25 Annual Report p3: 'Stanislaus and Merced counties continue to utilize the Teeter Plan.' Confirmed for BOTH counties spanning the SFID.
teeter.implication: Teeter advances 100% of levy; debt service insulated from delinquency.

900211CP6.verdict_basis: Concern DEFUSED by primary data. SFID No.1 is NOT a thin carve-out: its $9.09B AV is 76.7% of the $11.85B whole district, it is residential-majority (70% residential / 60% single-family), diversified (top-20 only 11.5%, max single taxpayer 2.35%), growing steadily (+42.7% 7yr, +3.8% latest), and carries only $39.5M of GO debt => SFID AV-to-debt ~230x (debt 0.44% of AV). Both spanning counties (Stanislaus, Merced) run Teeter, so debt service is advanced 100%. Clean SFID GO; the SFID-vs-whole-district risk we couldn't see is now seen and is benign.
